quarterly_data.quarter: Moore Threads annual report: 2025 Annual Report (04-27-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: MTT S5000 (fourth-generation 'Pinghu' architecture) delivers up to 1,000 TFLOPS dense AI compute per card with 80GB of memory, 1.6TB/s memory bandwidth and about 800GB/s card-to-card interconnect; in 2025 the KUAE 10,000-card cluster built on it was commercially deployed, reaching 10 Exa-Flops. Moore Threads completed deep adaptation of full DeepSeek-V3/R1 on the S5000 using FP8 and Day-0 adaptation of Alibaba's Qwen and Wan and Zhipu models. The company says the 'Lushan' graphics chip on its 'Huagang' architecture will raise AAA-game rendering 15x, AI performance 64x and ray-tracing performance 50x. In 2025 it launched its first smart SoC, 'Changjiang' (50 TOPS heterogeneous AI compute), the MTT AIBOOK built on it (sold on JD.com) and the MTT E300 edge AI module (50 TOPS INT8, up to 64GB LPDDR5/5X at 136GB/s).
quarterly_data.figure: S5000: 1,000 TFLOPS dense, 80GB, 1.6TB/s; KUAE cluster 10 Exa-Flops

quarterly_data.quarter: Moore Threads annual report: 2025 Annual Report (04-27-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: R&D investment RMB 1,305,026,191.16 in 2025 (-3.95%), 86.68% of revenue, none capitalised; 1,009 R&D staff (79.20% of employees). 2025 spend on projects in development: Huashan chip RMB 28,793.29 ten-thousand, Pinghu 1S chip RMB 18,779.83 ten-thousand, Lushan chip RMB 13,859.54 ten-thousand, Pinghu chip RMB 11,295.23 ten-thousand, Changjiang chip RMB 9,671.80 ten-thousand and a new-generation inference chip RMB 1,265.15 ten-thousand; KUAE cluster R&D was completed. IPO-funded projects - a new-generation AI training-inference chip (RMB 235,745.32 ten-thousand planned), a new-generation graphics chip (RMB 235,064.50 ten-thousand) and a new-generation AI SoC chip (RMB 186,166.96 ten-thousand) - are scheduled to reach usable state in December 2028.

quarterly_data.quarter: Moore Threads annual report: 2025 Annual Report (04-27-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Company plan (2025 annual report): bring the 'Huagang' architecture and later generations to mass production and market, raising per-card compute density and efficiency; build a self-controlled technology base for 100,000-card clusters and move them toward engineered, large-scale deployment; accelerate SoC iteration for edge and terminal devices. The company says it will keep iterating chip architectures rapidly to narrow the technology and product gap with international leaders.
